title: Latency Slice Adapter and Progressive Shed Policy for Dedicated Fleets
creator: Asha Kapoor
description: Implement a latency-centric admission/queueing adapter that slices incoming traffic into latency tiers (fast/standard/batch) and applies progressive, SLO-aware shedding when capacity is constrained. This ticket covers the core routing adapter, tokenized admission for slices, and a shedding policy that ramps degradation from non-blocking defer->partial-response->reject while integrating autoscaler signals.
background: Dedicated fleets currently use bucketed priority lanes and token-based admission, but we observe that mixed workloads with divergent latency targets (interactive chat vs async summarization) cause tail latency regressions for high-priority tenants during bursts. Current approaches either over-provision or rely on blunt preemption. We need a slice-based admission layer that enforces per-slice throughput guarantees, gracefully degrades lower-priority slices, and cooperates with the autoscaler to reduce oscillation.
design_summary: Create an adapter component in the ingress pipeline that: 1) classifies requests into slices based on route metadata and SLA (fast/standard/batch); 2) maintains per-slice token buckets with configurable min-guarantee and burst-credit; 3) exposes a progressive shed state machine (OK -> DEFER -> TRUNCATE/REDUCE_TOKENS -> REJECT) driven by slice headroom and global fleet utilization; 4) emits metrics and autoscaler hints (expected shortfall) and supports config overrides via route-level policies. The adapter uses a small in-memory ring for short-term queueing and a bounded slowpath for longer waits. Admission decisions are deterministic by request hash to reduce unfairness under churn.
implementation_tasks: Spec: add latency-slice enum to API schema and migration plan
Ingress: implement SliceClassifier middleware (route rules + tenant hints)
Admission: per-slice token allocator with min_guarantee and burst_credit accounting
Shedding: implement progressive_shed state machine and hookpoints for partial-output/fallback
Queueing: bounded headroom ring + slowpath queue with time decay and backpressure signals
Autoscaler integration: emit shortfall and headroom metrics; consume scale-up cooldown hints
E2E tests: injection tests for slice isolation, burst scenarios, and degradation ordering
Dashboard & alerts: per-slice latency, rejects, deferred count; add runbook links
Docs: runtime config options and operational playbook for tuning slice params
rollout_plan: Phase 1: internal dogfood in staging with low-traffic tenant groups. Phase 2: enable for a subset of Dedicated fleets with conservative min_guarantees and verbose metrics. Phase 3: incrementally increase guarantees and enable progressive shedding. Feature flags gate classifier and shedding state machine. Rollback: switch classifier to passthrough and restore previous admission config.
monitoring_and_alerts: shortname: slice_p95_latency_exceeding_slo -> page if fast slice p95 > target for 5m
shortname: slice_reject_rate_spike -> warn if rejects/sec > threshold for any slice
shortname: progressive_shed_transitions -> track frequency of DEFER->REJECT transitions
autoscaler_hint_anomaly -> alert if emitted shortfall signals are sustained without scale actions
acceptance_criteria: Requests are classified into latency slices according to route metadata and tenant annotations
Per-slice min_guarantee respected under steady-state load in staging (validated by load tests)
Under burst, lower-priority slices enter DEFER then TRUNCATE before REJECT and fast slice p95 remains within target
Autoscaler receives shortfall hints and scale actions reduce shed events in subsequent window in >90% test runs
Logs and dashboards show per-slice metrics and a linkable trace id for admitted vs shed requests
Unit and integration tests cover deterministic admission decision logic and state transitions
